# Content Creation 101

> A free knowledge base about growing online with content: personal brand, hooks, storytelling, psychology of attention, packaging and virality, formats and video, articles, distribution, systems and AI, making money, and writing. 176 lessons in 11 modules, sorted from 65 videos and articles by top creators

Every lesson uses the same sections: Big idea, How it works, Steps, Examples, Where creators disagree, Mistakes, Try it. Each module ends with a cheat sheet. Creators are credited in CREDITS.md, the lessons themselves name no one

## Modules

- [Module 1: Personal brand and positioning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/01-personal-brand-and-positioning.md): Decide what you want to be known for, prove it, repeat it, and give it time. Lessons: Why personal brands work so well now; Start from the end: what you want to be known for; Proof first: do the thing, then talk about it; What a brand really is: a link in people's minds; Niche: start narrow, then widen; Size your niche: core, casual and new viewers; Positioning: promise, proof, perspective, personality; Contrarian takes and a point of view; Finding your gap and your advantage; Being real, your story and who you are; Worldbuilding: a world your audience lives in; Trust: how it is built and how to protect it; Obsession, stickiness and fans; A brand that lasts in the AI era; Plans, timelines and staying power
- [Module 2: Hooks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/02-hooks.md): Write openings that stop the scroll, make your topic clear in a second, and make the right people want the next line. Lessons: What a hook does and why it decides everything; The master formula: lean, stun, snap back; Five fast tips: visuals, benefits, familiar references, speed, short sentences; The six hook formats; The four parts of a hook and the key visual; The six word slots inside a hook; Hook mistakes 1 and 2: delay and confusion; Hook mistakes 3 and 4: irrelevance and disinterest; Text hooks and the first frame; After the hook: keep the promise, give the answer at the right time; Copy, understand, improve: building hook and keyword banks; The hook toolkit: proof, promise, plan; A hook system for X posts; Hooks in writing: first lines for posts, threads and articles; Hooks across platforms, long form and testing
- [Module 3: Storytelling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/03-storytelling.md): Storytelling is a skill you can learn: give people a reason to care, a question to guess and a surprise. Lessons: Why stories work; Context plus conflict; Zoom into the moment; Surprise and emotion; Stakes and the big question; Head fakes and re-hooks; Captivation, anticipation, validation; Making boring topics feel new; Short stories: the 60-second story, HPC and tension; Craft: rhythm, tone, direction and your angle; Storytelling mistakes and the story ladder; Finding, writing and editing your stories; Your brand as a story; Trust through transformation, losses and takeaways
- [Module 4: Psychology and attention](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/04-psychology-and-attention.md): People scroll without thinking, so learn what makes them stop, what makes them care and what makes them act. Lessons: Why people stop scrolling, and why they stay; The attention span myth; Dopamine: why not knowing the ending keeps people watching; The 6 steps from first glance to loyal viewer; Curiosity: the gap and the open loop; Newness: why the brain stops for new things; Making old ideas feel new; Emotion: what drives clicks, shares and action; Association, familiarity and liking; Trust, weakness and proof; Identity, sharing, common enemies and disagreement; Influence: the 7 R's, and persuading people who aren't looking; Persuasion shortcuts, certainty and the pull of a plan; Faces, constant change, and what people remember; How X picks what to show: one creator's reading of the algorithm
- [Module 5: Ideas, packaging and virality](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/05-ideas-packaging-and-virality.md): Pick ideas people already want, package them so people click, and make more of what wins. Lessons: What makes an idea go viral; Topic is king; Where good ideas come from; What an idea is made of: topic, angle, format; Making old topics feel new; Copy the format, not the content; Finding outliers; Breaking down outliers; Choosing which ideas to make; Why packaging decides the result; Thumbnails: simple, clear, one click; Titles that get the click; Viral writing 101; How the algorithm decides (and what creators disagree on); The X algorithm: 16 rules; The viral trap: chase the right views; Doing more of what works, and testing new things; Making things worth spreading; One big video instead of 10 normal ones, and the 3 stages of packaging
- [Module 6: Formats and video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/06-formats-and-video.md): Pick a few formats you can keep making, build the hook around what people see first, keep production simple, and post at a pace you can keep. Lessons: Choosing your formats; Ready-made formats to borrow; Short videos vs long videos; Writing a video hook: four layers and the key visual; The first frame and visual hooks; Short video structures; Long video structure: openings and sections; Pacing and keeping people watching; Scripts, outlines and script length; Filming: delivery, setting and simple production; Editing and giving editors feedback; How often to post: volume, quality and batching; A fast-growth plan for short videos; One idea, many platforms: reusing and order; AI in video production and editing; Viewer satisfaction: give what the title and thumbnail promised
- [Module 7: Articles and long-form writing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/07-articles-and-long-form-writing.md): Long pieces build trust. Pick a fresh topic, open with proof and a clear promise, make the article easy to scan, then push it after you publish. Lessons: Why long content builds trust; Choosing what the article is about; Titles and first lines; The opening, part 1: earning trust; The opening, part 2: attention and clarity; Five opening recipes; A 12-part article skeleton, top to bottom; Inside a section: text boxes and teaching moves; How top article authors structure the whole piece; Drafting, AI help and your own taste; The newsletter as your home base; Pacing and structure borrowed from long video advice; Pushing an article after it is published
- [Module 8: Distribution and growth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/08-distribution-and-growth.md): Get people to see your work, then turn their attention into trust, an audience you own, and sales. Lessons: The one rule of growth: get people to see your work; Interest media: how apps pick who sees you; How the X algorithm works, as creators read it; Growing on X: what to do and what to avoid; Choosing your platforms; How often and when to post; Replies, comments and networking; Borrowing reach: quotes, remixes, collabs and group chats; Reusing content: the waterfall versus the lake; Do more of what works; Building an audience that spreads you; Own your audience: connect your channels; Patience, practice and not quitting; Starting from zero: niche, bio, voice and category; Why the most-viewed article in X history worked; From views to money: the attention conversion funnel; An audience of buyers; Content that sells: the $10,000 test and how often to promote; Content campaigns and the funnel by audience stage; Launches and creator collabs; Growth phases for a company, and founders with no audience; Go to market: pick channels by how you sell; Outbound email, SEO and ads
- [Module 9: Systems, teams and AI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/09-systems-teams-and-ai.md): Build a system and a team so your content keeps going without you doing everything. Lessons: Why a system works better than waiting for inspiration; The content workflow loop; Idea banks and swipe files; Filtering ideas: the funnel and the meeting where you cut ideas; Measuring what counts; How often to review: learning from your best posts; Simplify before you automate; AI as a helper: speed from AI, judgment from you; Building an AI content team; Team levels: who to hire and when; Hiring and running your team day to day; Lead your creative team instead of controlling it; Safe to fail: bad results, hackathons and training; Being a leader worth following; Burnout, focus time and creative structure; Team standards: principles, details and values
- [Module 10: Money and careers in content](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/10-money-and-careers-in-content.md): Attention turns into money when people trust you, you have something to sell, and buying is easy. Lessons: Why content turns into money; All the ways to make money from content; Give first, sell later; Give away your best ideas, sell the help with using them; Your first product: small, fast, tested; The micro service: 4 coaching calls; Getting your first client by hand; Sales conversations, follow-up and the email list; The funnel: from stranger to buyer; Building an offer from zero, and a 90-day plan; Sales page structure and guarantees; Careers in content: showing your value, and hiring; A selling system: customers, trust and an audience you own; CTAs, offers and big moments; A career path: becoming the person brands hire; A career path: becoming a creative director; Career principles for getting ahead
- [Module 11: Writing and copywriting](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/guide/11-writing-and-copywriting.md): Write clear, specific, human words that get the right reader to take the right action. Lessons: What good copy actually is; Clear over clever: smart ideas, simple words; Make every sentence clear; Every word earns its place; Be specific: numbers, names and proof; Use the words your audience already uses; Open, close and shape a post; Contrast, tension and an honest tone; Persuasive copy: six checks and better headlines; CTAs and persuasion in every format; Voice: write like you talk; Speak to one person: how to talk on camera; Explain simply, and keep AI sounding human

## Tools

- [The Personal Brand Playbook](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-tek/Content-Creation-101/main/PLAYBOOK.md): 17 steps in order, each with a goal, questions to answer, rules, mistakes and the lessons it comes from
